method: BASELINE. Written straight from the deposited texts with the writing-l4-rules skill, from the seat of the individual to whom the law is applied, with the design defaults ruled on 2026-10-18; the Act's Part IV read with the Regulations 2020 (reg 10, reg 11 (2), Schedule 1), which set its numbers and dates; a seat-neutral core (maib-core.l4, with three regulative rules: reg 10 (2)-(4) for the claimant, s 28 (1)-(2) and s 23 (1), (1A), (2) for the Board), the individual's seat layer (maib-seat.l4) and the Board's seat layer limited to its s 23 duty to pay (maib-seat-board.l4), neither restating a rule; mirror cases for the two seats; no REFUSE (an accident before 17 February 2020 for the allowances, the cap and the death benefit, funeral benefits for an accident before 1 December 2007, and a s 6 (1) conviction below 0.05 answer `not covered`, asserted); checked with the stable l4 of VS Code extension 1.6.98, JL4_LIBRARY_PATH unset. No pipeline, no coverage table, no independent test pass, no human gate.
edition_encoded: Motor Accidents (Liabilities and Compensation) Act 1973 (No. 71 of 1973), consolidated version published 2026-01-28, current on Tasmanian Legislation Online at 2026-10-20, as deposited at ../../registers/source-bundle/act-1973-071.txt; with the Motor Accidents (Liabilities and Compensation) Regulations 2020 (S.R. 2020, No. 7), consolidated version published 2021-06-15, current at 2026-10-20, as deposited at ../../../motor-accidents-liabilities-and-compensation-regulations-2020/registers/source-bundle/sr-2020-007.txt (the Sch 1 Pt 3 cl 2 (1) funeral formula as transcribed from its image in the deposit)

checks.l4: stable l4 of VS Code extension legalese.l4-vscode 1.6.98, JL4_LIBRARY_PATH unset
checks.command: l4 run maib-core.l4 ; l4 run maib-seat.l4 ; l4 run maib-seat-board.l4 ; l4 run maib-cases-injured.l4 ; l4 run maib-cases-board.l4
checks.result: 242 assertions satisfied, 0 errors, 0 warnings (2026-10-24); 4 #TRACEs with an expect line (2 breaches by the claimant under reg 10 (2), 2 obligations pending: the Board's s 23 payment of the exact amount, and the claimant's s 28 (2) permission), each read and as expected; calendar dates checked independently with Python's datetime
checks.note: l4 run exits 0 even when an assertion fails, so the diagnostics are what was read.

scope: In: Act s 2 (1) (interstate motor vehicle, interstate premium, motor accident, daily care, registered), s 2 (4), s 2 (5), s 2B (resident), s 23 (1), (1AA), (1A), (2), (2A)-(2C), (3), (8) (the duty to pay; family member), s 24 (1) (a)-(h) and (1A), (2), (3), (3A), (4), (4A) (exclusions; the alcohol table), s 26 (no regulation made), s 27A (2)-(6), s 28 (1)-(2); Regulations reg 10 (2)-(4) (notice and claim, Tribunal extension), reg 11 (2) (prescribed trailers), Sch 1 Pt 1 (definitions, dependants, dependent child, survivorship, cl 8 cap), Pt 2 (medical benefits, taxi and travel), Pt 3 (funeral benefits), Pt 4 cl 1 (1)-(4) and cl 2 (death benefits from 17 February 2020), Pt 5 (disability allowances: employed, self-employed, housekeeping; periods; limits; average weekly earnings), Pt 7 (counselling). Out: Part III (common-law liability, the Board's third-party indemnity, ss 14-22), Part V premiums, Parts II and IIA (Board administration, the Injury Prevention and Management Foundation), s 24 (5), s 25, s 27 except s 27A, s 27B, ss 28A-28C, Sch 1 Pt 6 in detail (only the cl 8 cap counts it), death and funeral benefits for accidents before 17 February 2020 and 1 December 2007 (the 2010 and 2000 Regulations, not deposited), regs 1-9. Read with subjects/au/social-security-act-1991 (compensation recovery, Part 3.14), subjects/au/income-tax-assessment-act-1997 (allowances as ordinary income, s 6-5), subjects/au/health-insurance-act-1973 (Medicare amounts netted off under Pt 2 cl 1 (2)) and subjects/au/tas/workers-rehabilitation-and-compensation-act-1988 (s 24 (1) (b)); cross-folder IMPORT is not possible.
seats: the injured person (and the dependants and personal representative of a person killed in a motor accident, and the family members claiming counselling services benefits)
the Motor Accidents Insurance Board as insurer, only for its duty to pay scheduled benefits under s 23 (1), (1A) and (2)
